info.title: FormFav Racing API
info.description:
## FormFav Racing API

Access horse racing data, analysis, and predictions.

### Authentication

All endpoints (except /health) require authentication via API key.

Include your API key in the `X-API-Key` header:
```
X-API-Key: your_api_key_here
```

### Getting Started

1. **Create an account** at [formfav.com](https://formfav.com) — free, no credit card required.
2. **Generate an API key** from the *Get API Key* button in the site header once you're
   signed in. Copy it immediately — the raw key is shown once.
3. **Send it on every request** via the `X-API-Key` header:
```
X-API-Key: your_api_key_here
```
4. **Make your first call** — try `GET /v1/form?date=YYYY-MM-DD&track=SLUG&race=NUM`.

For a step-by-step walkthrough, see the [Quickstart guide](https://formfav.com/docs/quickstart).

> **Note:** Accounts are managed through formfav.com (Replit OAuth). The
> `/v1/auth/register` and `/v1/auth/login` endpoints exist for service-to-service
> use and shouldn't be called directly — registering this way creates an account
> that isn't linked to your formfav.com login, Stripe subscription, or trial.

### Access Levels

- **free**: Essential racing data to get started (1,000 req/day)
- **pro**: Full data access with speed maps, class profiles and form badges (20,000 req/day)
- **premium**: Everything in Pro plus live prices and real-time results (100,000 req/day)
- **enterprise**: Unlimited access with priority support

### Rate Limits

Limits are per account over a **rolling 24-hour window** (each request stops counting
24 hours after it was made; there is no midnight reset), shared by all your API keys
and connected apps. Every authenticated `GET` response carries:

- `X-RateLimit-Limit-Day` — your limit per 24 hours, or `unlimited`
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining-Day` — requests you can make right now: your limit minus every
  request counted in the last 24 hours. Counts refresh about once a minute, so it can
  trail your latest requests by up to a minute. Not sent on unlimited plans.

A `429` carries `Retry-After`, the seconds until requests are accepted again: for the
daily limit, until enough of your requests age out of the window; for the short burst
limit, 10 seconds. `GET /v1/usage` returns the same numbers as JSON without counting
against the quota. See [Rate Limiting](https://formfav.com/docs/rate-limiting).

### Typical API Workflow

1. `GET /v1/form/meetings?date=YYYY-MM-DD` — list today's meetings by race type
2. `GET /v1/form?date=...&track=...&race=N` — get the full race form for a specific race
3. `GET /v1/predictions?date=...&track=...&race=N` — win/place probabilities (Pro)
4. `GET /v1/stats/track-bias/{track}` — barrier/box bias context (Pro)
5. `GET /v1/stats/jockey/{name}` or `/trainer/{name}` — person stats (Pro)
6. `GET /v1/stats/runner/{id}` — full runner career profile (Pro)

Use `/v1/form/venues` to discover valid track names and `/v1/stats/jockey/search`,
`/v1/stats/trainer/search`, `/v1/stats/runner/search` to resolve names before calling
detail endpoints.

### Key Concepts

- **race_code**: `gallops` (thoroughbred, default), `harness`, or `greyhounds`
- **track**: Use slug format from `/v1/form/venues` (e.g. `flemington`, `eagle-farm`)
- **Date window**: every dated endpoint serves 30 days ago to 7 days ahead
- **Stats data window**: Career statistics are computed from approximately 2019 onwards
- Stats sub-fields (e.g. `trackStats`, `conditionStats`) may be `null` when sample size is below threshold
- Predictions `winProb` is normalised to sum to 1.0 across all non-scratched runners; `placeProb` is the chance of finishing in the places paid (top 3 with 8+ runners, top 2 with 5–7), so it sums to the number of places

get.description:
Current prices for a single race.

A race with no live market returns 200 with empty `prices` lists rather than
404 — "the market is not up yet" is a real answer, and a 404 would be pinned by
the edge's negative cache and outlive the condition.

get.description:
Get race form data for a specific race.

Returns the full race form including all runners with their details:
- Runner number, name, jockey, trainer
- Weight, barrier, age
- Recent form and career statistics
- Scratching status
- **Speed map data** (Pro/Enterprise tier only)

**Parameters:**
- **date**: Race date in YYYY-MM-DD format (required)
- **track**: Track/venue name - use slug format like 'flemington' or 'royal-randwick' (required)
- **race**: Race number 1-15 (required)
- **race_code**: Race type - gallops (default), harness, or greyhounds
- **country**: Country code - au (default); also nz, hk, gb, ie, fr, us, jp and others (see Country enum)
- **timezone**: IANA timezone scoping the `date` window (default: Australia/Sydney)

**Date Range:**
- Minimum: 30 days in the past
- Maximum: 7 days in the future

**Pro Tier Features:**
- `speedMap` field for each rated runner: running style, early speed index and settling
  position. What they are built from differs by race code (harness early speed is
  draw-adjusted and its settling position is the bell); see the SpeedMapData schema
- `classProfile` field with runner's class rating profile (current, peak, optimal range)
- `raceClassFit` field showing how the runner fits this race's class level

**Example:**
```
GET /v1/form?date=2025-01-15&track=flemington&race=7
```

get.description:
Get list of meetings for a date and race type.

Returns all meetings for the date (AU, NZ, HK, GB, IE, FR, US, JP and others),
including whether a meeting was abandoned. Every caller gets the full international
set — filter client-side on the `country` field of each meeting.

Meetings with `abandoned: true` should generally be skipped — form data may still be
available but race results will not exist.

**Parameters:**
- **date**: Race date in YYYY-MM-DD format (required)
- **race_code**: Race type - gallops (default), harness, or greyhounds
- **timezone**: IANA timezone scoping the `date` window (default: Australia/Sydney)

**Example:**
```
GET /v1/form/meetings?date=2025-01-15&race_code=gallops
```

get.description:
Get win/place probability predictions for a race.

**Pro tier and above.**
- **Premium and Enterprise** get the most advanced prediction model, and a
  race's predictions as soon as its field is published.
- **Pro** gets predictions for today's and tomorrow's races (Sydney time).
  Asking for a later race that Premium already has answers 403.

Returns probability scores for each runner based on ML models:
- **winProb**: Win probability (0-1)
- **placeProb**: Place probability (0-1): top 3 with 8+ runners, top 2 with 5-7,
  the win probability with 4 or fewer
- **modelRank**: Model's ranking prediction (1 = best chance)
- **confidence**: Model confidence level (high, medium, low)
- **predictedAt**: When this version was made (UTC)

Scratched runners are removed. On Premium and Enterprise that includes live
scratchings, the same ones their race card shows. `winProb` then sums to 1.0 across the runners left;
`placeProb` is derived from those win probabilities and sums to the number of places
paid. Predictions are only generated for races with sufficient runner data — not all
races will have predictions available.

Supported race types: gallops (thoroughbred), harness, and greyhounds.

**Parameters:**
- **date**: Race date in YYYY-MM-DD format (required), within the last 30 days to 7 days ahead
- **track**: Track/venue name (required)
- **race**: Race number 1-12 (required)
- **race_code**: Race type - gallops (default), harness, or greyhounds
- **country**: Country code - au (default)
- **timezone**: IANA timezone scoping the `date` window (default: Australia/Sydney)

**Example:**
```
GET /v1/predictions?date=2026-01-24&track=randwick&race=8
```

get.description:
Get the result for a specific race.

**Pro tier only** - requires active Pro or Enterprise subscription.

Takes the same parameters as `/form`, so a race you fetched form for can be
looked up here with the identical query string.

**Market coverage:** every market `/form` covers. Where the batch pipeline has a
results source (Australia, New Zealand gallops, Hong Kong, GB/IE) results arrive with
it; elsewhere the confirmed result from the bookmaker results feeds is served once the
race is two hours past its start (Premium sees it as it lands).

Returns each runner with their finishing position and margin, ordered by
result — finishers first, then non-finishers, then scratchings:
- **position**: finishing position, 1 = winner. Present only for runners that
  completed the race, and **omitted** otherwise. Dead heats legitimately share
  a position, so it is not unique within a race.
- **scratched**: `true` for withdrawn runners, which never have a position.

Between them those two cover every case. A runner with a `position` ran and
finished there; one with `scratched: true` was withdrawn; one with neither has
no result — either it did not finish, or the result has not landed yet. Use
`resultStatus` to tell those apart: in a `final` race every unscratched runner
has been resulted, so one still lacking a position did not finish.
- **margin**: cumulative margin behind the winner as recorded by the source.
  Greyhounds carry a metres suffix (`"4.25m"`); gallops and harness are
  lengths with no unit (`"1.7"`). The winner reads `"0"`/`"0.0"`. Omitted
  where there is no result.
- **startingPrice**: official starting price as decimal odds — `4.50` means
  $4.50 returned on a $1 win stake, stake included. Taken from the racing
  body's own published result, not from a wagering operator, and settled
  after the race: **this is not a live or pre-race price and never moves.**
  **Coverage is partial and this key is omitted whenever we do not hold a
  price** — it is absent for NZ harness entirely and still filling elsewhere,
  so do not assume every runner in a race carries one, and do not treat an
  absent price as a scratching or a zero.

**resultStatus** describes the race as a whole:
- `final` — every unscratched runner has a result
- `interim` — results are partially in
- `pending` — nothing yet (the race may not have been run)
- `abandoned` — the race was abandoned; no result will ever exist

A race that exists but has not been resulted returns **200 with
`resultStatus: "pending"`**, not 404. 404 means the race itself was not found.

**Freshness depends on your tier.** On Pro, results are ingested by a pipeline
run every 2-3 hours, not streamed — expect a lag between a race finishing and
its result appearing. On **Premium/Enterprise** the same request additionally
returns live `prices` per runner and fills in results from the real-time feed
before the batch run catches up. No parameter or URL change is needed; the
payload follows the key.

**prices** (Premium/Enterprise): a list with one entry per bookmaker, ordered by
bookmaker name, each carrying `bookmaker`, `win` / `place` decimal odds and its
own `capturedAt` (books update independently, so freshness is per-bookmaker, not
per-runner). A bookmaker offering neither market is omitted rather than sent with
nulls, the whole field is omitted for a runner with no usable prices, and it is
omitted entirely on tiers without real-time access — so a Pro payload is exactly
as it was before prices existed. Quotes older than the staleness threshold are
dropped rather than served as current. No "best price" is computed; rank the
list yourself if you need one.

**Date Range:**
- Minimum: 30 days in the past (configurable)
- Maximum: 7 days in the future

**Example:**
```
GET /v1/results?date=2026-07-23&track=northam&race=1
```

get.description:
Get results for every race at a meeting, in race-number order.

**Market coverage:** every market `/form` covers — see `/results` for how results
arrive in markets without a batch results source.

**Pro tier only** - requires active Pro or Enterprise subscription.

One call instead of looping `/results` over race numbers. Each entry in
`races` is the same object `/results` returns for that race — including the
optional `startingPrice` per runner, on the same partial-coverage terms
described there — so races still awaiting results appear with
`resultStatus: "pending"` rather than being omitted; the card is always
complete.

Use `/form/meetings` first to discover which tracks ran on a date.

**Example:**
```
GET /v1/results/meeting?date=2026-07-23&track=northam
```

get.description:
Search for jockey canonical names matching a partial query.

Use this before calling `/stats/jockey/{name}` to discover the exact canonical
name to use, especially when unsure of spelling or given name vs nickname.

Returns matches ordered by total career starts (most active jockeys first).
The `isAmbiguous` flag indicates the name could not be confidently resolved
to a single person (e.g. "J. McDonald" with multiple possible full names).

**Example:**
```
GET /v1/stats/jockey/search?q=mcdonald&race_code=gallops
```

get.description:
Get track-by-track performance statistics for a jockey.

**Pro tier only** - requires active Pro subscription.

Use `/stats/jockey/search?q=name` first to find the exact canonical name.

Returns statistics including:
- **totalStarts**: Career total rides (data window from ~2019 onwards, not full career)
- **totalWins**: Career wins (same window)
- **overallWinRate**: Overall win percentage
- **trackStats**: Performance breakdown by track (venue, wins, win rate, etc.)
- **isAmbiguous**: True if the name could match multiple jockeys

**Note:** `totalStarts` reflects the available data window (~2019 onwards), not the
jockey's full career. Per-venue breakdowns in `trackStats` use the same window.

**Parameters:**
- **jockey_name**: Jockey name (case-insensitive, supports partial match)
- **race_code**: Race type - gallops (default) or harness

**Example:**
```
GET /v1/stats/jockey/James%20McDonald?race_code=gallops
```

Get the full statistics profile for a runner.

**Pro tier only** - requires active Pro subscription.

Use `/stats/runner/search?q=name` first to find the runner ID.

Returns the complete profile including:
- **runner**: Identity (name, sire, dam, country, age)
- **career**: Career summary (starts, wins, win rate)
- **distanceStats**: Performance by distance
- **conditionStats**: Performance by track condition (full career scope)
- **trackDistanceStats**: Performance by track+distance combo
- **spellStats**: First-up, second-up performance (R/H only)
- **boxStats**: Box performance (greyhounds only)
- **jockeyStats**: Jockey partnerships (R/H only)
- **classProfile**: Class rating profile
- **weightProfile**: Weight analysis (thoroughbreds only)
- **runningStyle**: Running style summary

**Note:** `conditionStats` uses full career scope while `career.starts`, `distanceStats`,
and `trackDistanceStats` use the ~2019 data window. Totals across these sections may not
add up. Any stats section may be `null` if the sample size is below the minimum threshold.

**Example:**
```
GET /v1/stats/runner/12345?window=90
```

schema.description: Optional rolling window in days (14–365). When provided, recentStats is populated.

parameters.description: Optional rolling window in days (14–365). When provided, recentStats is populated.

get.description:
Get barrier bias statistics for a track.

**Pro tier only** - requires active Pro subscription.

Returns statistics including:
- **expectedWinRate**: Expected win rate if no bias (based on field size)
- **barrierStats**: Performance by barrier position with advantage calculation
- **strongestBarrier**: Barrier with highest win rate
- **weakestBarrier**: Barrier with lowest win rate
- **biasStrength**: Overall bias severity (none, mild, moderate, strong)

The **advantage** field shows percentage points above/below expected:
- Positive = favorable barrier (wins more than expected)
- Negative = unfavorable barrier (wins less than expected)

For greyhounds, barrier numbers represent box positions (1-8).

**Distance:**
- By default **distanceStats** breaks the track down into distance bands
  (gallops: Sprint/Mile/Middle/Classic/Staying/Marathon; harness:
  Mile/Middle/Staying/Long; greyhounds: Sprint/Medium/Distance), each with
  its own barrier table, strongest/weakest barrier and bias strength.
- Pass **distance** to scope the whole report to one distance (`1200`) or a
  custom range (`1200-1600`). The top-level barrierStats, strongestBarrier,
  weakestBarrier and biasStrength then describe only those races,
  **distanceFilter** echoes the range, and distanceStats holds a single
  `Custom` entry for the slice whose minDistance/maxDistance are the
  distances actually run inside the range. recentStats (when window is
  given) is scoped the same way.

Barriers with fewer than 5 starts in a scoped or per-band view are omitted.

**Parameters:**
- **track**: Track/venue name (e.g. 'flemington', 'randwick')
- **race_code**: Race type - gallops (default), harness, or greyhounds
- **country**: Country code (default: au)
- **distance**: Metres, `1200` or `1200-1600` (200–5000)

**Examples:**
```
GET /v1/stats/track-bias/flemington?race_code=gallops
GET /v1/stats/track-bias/randwick?distance=1200
GET /v1/stats/track-bias/randwick?distance=1400-1600&window=90
```

Derived only from current fixed-odds quotes (stale and tote quotes are left out) and

in-running or post-race prices, not a pre-race market. Omitted when no runner has a
current price.

The field is every runner not scratched, except that a runner none of the pricing
bookmakers quotes, when there are enough of them to quote a consensus, is treated as
out of the race: a dual acceptor running elsewhere, or a scratching our card has not
caught yet.

For a result filled in from the real-time feed it is when that feed last reported. **Omitted** when we hold no change record — every race resulted before change-tracking began — so absence means 'unknown', never 'unchanged'.

A result usually lands in more than one (placings, then margins), so a value above 1 does NOT mean it was corrected — use `resultRevised` for that. Use it to order two copies of the same race: the higher number is later. Omitted under the same conditions as `resultUpdatedAt`, and always for a result served from the real-time feed, which keeps no history.

RunnerForm.title: RunnerForm
RunnerForm.description:
Individual runner in a race.

NOTE: Do not expose internal fields that could reveal data sources,
such as form_comment, source_id, or raw scraper data.

decorators.description: Form trending upward with strong recent results
decorators.label: In Form

bookmakers.title: Bookmakers
bookmakers.description: Bookmakers with a current fixed win price for this runner. Brands that share one trading book (Coral and Ladbrokes UK) count once.

best.title: Best
best.description: Longest current fixed win price across bookmakers.

consensus.title: Consensus
consensus.description: Median current win price across bookmakers, margin included. Needs enough bookmakers quoting this runner: any 3, or 2 of the market leaders where the race is run (TAB, Ladbrokes and Sportsbet in Australia, New Zealand and Hong Kong; Ladbrokes UK, which Coral shares, and William Hill in the UK, Ireland and Europe; Bet365 everywhere). One leader and one other is not enough.

fair.title: Fair
fair.description: Margin-free win odds (1 / fairProbability). Present only when enough bookmakers (as for `consensus`) each price every runner still in the race.

fairProbability.title: Fairprobability
fairProbability.description: Margin-free win probability (0-1); sums to 1 across the field. Each complete book is devigged by the power method, which takes more of the margin out of longshots than favourites (the favourite-longshot bias), then the books' probabilities are combined by median.

edge.title: Edge
edge.description: best x fairProbability - 1: the return per unit staked at the best price if fairProbability is right. Positive means the best price is longer than fair. Present with `fair`.

rank.title: Rank
rank.description: Market rank by fairProbability, 1 = favourite. Equal chances share a rank. Present with `fair`.

RunnerMarket.title: RunnerMarket
RunnerMarket.description: What the bookmakers say about one runner taken together, rather than book by book.

number.title: Number
number.description: Runner number (saddlecloth, or box for greyhounds)

scratched.title: Scratched
scratched.description: Withdrawn before the race. Sourced from our own race card, not inferred from a missing price — a bookmaker nulls a price for suspension and scratching alike, so the two are not distinguishable upstream.

prices.title: Prices
prices.description: One entry per bookmaker and market, ordered by bookmaker. Empty when every quote we hold is older than the staleness threshold for this race's time to jump — an empty list means 'nothing current', never 'no market'.

market.description: This runner's prices taken across bookmakers: best, consensus and fair. Omitted for a scratched runner, one with no current price, and every runner once the race is off.

RunnerPriceLine.title: RunnerPriceLine
RunnerPriceLine.description: One runner's quotes, with just enough identity to match it to a race card.

price.title: Price
price.description: Win price at this point (decimal odds)

at.title: At
at.description: When this price was published (UTC, ISO 8601)

RunnerPriceMovement.title: RunnerPriceMovement
RunnerPriceMovement.description:
One win price and the time the bookmaker published it.

`at` is the bookmaker's own timestamp, not our capture time, so points stay
correctly ordered across sources that poll at different rates and can be lined
up against the race start.

bookmaker.title: Bookmaker
bookmaker.description: Which bookmaker is offering this price (e.g. 'sportsbet'). Not the same as the upstream data provider.

marketType.title: Markettype
marketType.description: `fixed` or `tote`. One bookmaker can quote the same runner on both — TAB does — so a runner may carry two entries for the same bookmaker that differ only here.

open.title: Open
open.description: Opening win price. Omitted when this bookmaker does not publish one and the market opened before we first saw it.

close.title: Close
close.description: Last win price this bookmaker offered. While a market is still trading this tracks `win`; it stops moving when the book stops quoting, so after the jump it is the true closing price rather than becoming null with the market.

high.title: High
high.description: Longest (highest) win price seen — the 'top fluc'. Taken over every point known, including any evicted from `movements` by its length cap.

startingPrice.title: Startingprice
startingPrice.description: THIS BOOKMAKER's settled starting price — the price they settled win bets at. Not the same value as `startingPrice` on the runner itself, which is the racing body's official figure: these are per bookmaker, they disagree with each other, and they disagree with the official one. Present only once a race has settled and only for books that publish it.

movements.title: Movements
movements.description: Win-price movements, oldest first, most recent 20. Where a bookmaker publishes its own history this is that history — which reaches back to the market open, before we began polling. Otherwise it is what we observed, recorded only when the price actually changed, so consecutive entries always differ. Empty means no movement is known, never that the price has not moved.

stale.title: Stale
stale.description: True when this quote is older than the freshness allowance for this race, which tightens as the jump approaches and to ~2 minutes once it is off. A stale quote is SERVED, not withheld — `win` and `place` are omitted because they are claims about what you can bet right now, while `open`, `close`, `high`, `low` and `movements` are records of what happened and remain valid. Read `capturedAt` for the age. A finished race is therefore always stale, and that is not a coverage gap.

capturedAt.title: Capturedat
capturedAt.description: When the source observed this bookmaker's price (UTC, ISO 8601). Per-bookmaker, because books update independently — use it to judge freshness yourself. Prices older than the staleness threshold are dropped rather than served as current.

RunnerPrices.title: RunnerPrices
RunnerPrices.description:
One bookmaker's live prices for a runner. **Premium/Enterprise only** —
omitted entirely for other tiers, so a Pro payload is byte-identical to what it
was before prices existed.

A runner carries one of these per bookmaker, since the point of the feed is to
show what each book is offering rather than a single consensus number. There is
deliberately no "best price" field: which book is best is a function of the list
the caller already has, and computing it here would make the response an
odds-comparison product rather than a data feed.

Decimal odds (e.g. 4.50 = $4.50). A market this book is not currently pricing is
omitted rather than sent as 0 — that covers suspension, never-offered, and the
runner being scratched, which the upstream feed does not distinguish. Use
`scratched` on the runner for scratchings; it comes from our own data.

barrier.title: Barrier
barrier.description: Barrier draw / box number. Harness: the place within the runner's row (startRow) or at its handicap mark (handicapMetres)

startRow.title: Startrow
startRow.description: Harness only: the row the runner starts from, 'front' or 'second'. With barrier (the place within that row) it is the start: startRow 'second' and barrier 1 is Sr1. Omitted for a back-mark runner in a standing start (see handicapMetres) and outside harness.

unruly.title: Unruly
unruly.description: Harness only: true when the runner is drawn in an unruly place in its row or at its mark ('FrU3', '20m U1' in the barrier text). Omitted outside harness.

handicapMetres.title: Handicapmetres
handicapMetres.description: Harness standing starts: metres behind the front mark (e.g. 20); barrier is then the place at that mark. Omitted for runners on the front mark, on mobile starts, and outside harness.

position.title: Position
position.description: Finishing position, 1 = winner. Present only for runners that completed the race — omitted for scratched, non-finishing and not-yet-resulted runners. Dead heats legitimately share a position, so this is not unique within a race.

margin.title: Margin
margin.description: Margin behind the winner, cumulative, as recorded by the source. Greyhounds carry a metres suffix (e.g. '4.25m'); gallops and harness are lengths with no unit (e.g. '1.7'). The winner reads '0'/'0.0'. Omitted when the runner has no result, and for non-finishers.

startingPrice.title: Startingprice
startingPrice.description: Official **settled** starting price as decimal odds (e.g. 4.50 means $4.50 returned for a $1 win stake, stake included). Sourced from the racing body's own published result, not from a wagering operator, and fixed after the race — it never moves. Distinct from `prices`, which is the live pre-race market and Premium-only. **Omitted whenever we do not hold one**, which is common: coverage is still filling and is absent entirely for NZ harness. Treat it as optional and never assume every runner in a race carries one.

resultStage.title: Resultstage
resultStage.description: How settled this runner's position is, when it came from the real-time feed rather than the batch pipeline. `interim` means provisional placings; `correct_weight` means stewards have confirmed. **Premium/Enterprise only, and only while the batch result is still catching up** — once the batch pipeline has the race, its position is used and this is omitted. Absent therefore means the position is the settled one, not that it is unconfirmed.

prices.title: Prices
prices.description: Live prices, one entry per bookmaker, ordered by bookmaker name. **Premium/Enterprise only** — absent on other tiers, and absent for any runner whose prices are all stale or unavailable. A bookmaker offering neither market is omitted from the list rather than sent with null prices. Distinct from `startingPrice`, which is the settled post-race figure available to all Pro callers.

RunnerResult.title: RunnerResult
RunnerResult.description:
A single runner's result in a race.

Identity fields (number, name, jockey, trainer, weight, claim, barrier) use
the same names and derivation as ``RunnerForm`` in models/form.py.

There is deliberately no ``outcome`` field. It used to carry
placed|did_not_finish|scratched|pending, but "placed" meant "completed the
race", which collides with the racing sense of finishing in the paying places
— a runner sixth of six reported ``outcome: "placed"``. ``position`` and
``scratched`` already say everything callers need, so the ambiguous field was
removed rather than renamed. ``RunnerOutcome`` still exists and is still
computed internally: it orders the placings and drives ``resultStatus``.

RunnerSearchResult.title: RunnerSearchResult

runningStyle.title: Runningstyle
runningStyle.description: Where the runner usually races: L (Leader), P (Presser), M (Midfield), B (Backmarker). Gallops: from the average settling position (L 2 or better, P to 5, M to 8, B behind). Greyhounds and harness: relative to the field over the last 20 starts, so about one rated runner in five is a Leader.

earlySpeedIndex.title: Earlyspeedindex
earlySpeedIndex.description: 0-10, higher = quicker early. Gallops and greyhounds: how far forward the runner usually is early. Harness: draw-adjusted - 5 is typical for the draws the horse has had, higher means it gets further forward than its draws predict - so a harness Leader that keeps drawing the front row can sit near 5.

settlingPosition.title: Settlingposition
settlingPosition.description: Average running position, 1 = leading. Gallops: at the first in-running call. Greyhounds: at the first call (a field-relative estimate where a track publishes no call places). Harness: at the bell, a mid-race position.

SpeedMapData.title: SpeedMapData
SpeedMapData.description:
Speed map data for a runner (Pro/Enterprise tier only), from its past starts.

Each code publishes different in-running data, so the fields are built from:
- Gallops: position at the first in-running call (where the horse settles).
- Greyhounds: place at the first call and first-sectional rank, relative to the field.
  UK tracks publish few call places, so UK dogs rest mostly on the first sectional.
- Harness: running order at the bell (start of the last lap) plus stewards'
  early-race notes. No early call is published, and the draw dominates, so
  earlySpeedIndex is adjusted for the draws the horse has had.

Omitted when the runner can't be rated: fewer than three starts with in-running
data, or a greyhound or harness jurisdiction whose in-running data doesn't yet
pass our quality checks (today: greyhounds in Australia and the UK, harness in
Australia).
